The spirit speaks plain, but I do not know this Wewush. No trader or hunter has brought word of them to our fire. 

You say they are hungry. How many mouths? How far do they walk? What do they have that we might need — stone, hide, skill, or only empty hands? 

Grain we have, yes. Enough to see us through two winters and still plant. But grain carried away is grain not in our granary when the lean weeks come. I will not promise what I cannot spare, nor send food into dark without knowing who receives it.

Tell me more, spirit. Or tell me how I might find them myself.

Joawethom. Never heard the name. No trader, no hunter, no traveller has spoken it at our fires.

You come in a dream and ask me to empty our granary for a village no one has seen. That is not how we do things. We trade with people we know, or we send envoys to find them first.

How would you know their bellies are empty? And why should I listen to a voice in the night over the word of my own eyes?

The wind carries many voices, spirit, and I do not bend my knee to every whisper.  
We have grain enough to feed our own for many seasons, yet we know nothing of this Wewush — where they dwell, what they have given us, or why they hunger now.  
Tell me: have they ever shared fish, hide, or knowledge with us?  What do they offer in return for the wheat you ask us to spare?

Joawethom. Never heard the name. My people know no other villages - we've sent no envoys, seen no traders, found no tracks but our own.

How do you know this place? How do you know they're hungry? And what do you want from me for this knowledge?
